target_body: Promo test: paid conversions +31%, monthly rev +18%, low-touch seg, later-cycle retention -12pp; support model unchanged throughout.
system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Promo test: paid conversions +31%, monthly rev +18%, low-touch seg, later-cycle retention -12pp; support model unchanged throughout.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

memory_block.body: Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.
Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.
Promo test: paid conversions +31%, monthly rev +18%, low-touch seg, later-cycle retention -12pp; support model unchanged throughout.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.
Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.
Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

answer.rationale:
Two of the three current problems are onboarding completion (-4% QoQ) and activation (-6% QoQ), and those are causally linked: onboarding completion feeds activation. Simplifying onboarding addresses the upstream constraint and is supported by two independent inherited records (memory_86 on shortened onboarding lifting completion and time-to-value, memory_31 on cutting required signup fields producing a durable SMB activation lift). Activation messaging (memory_91) is the runner-up but treats a symptom further downstream. I am explicitly declining promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 shows the tempting headline (+31% conversions, +18% monthly revenue) alongside later-cycle retention of -12pp with the support model unchanged, which is a direct trade of long-term qualified revenue for short-term volume and conflicts with the stated primary objective. Matching a price attack in the exact segment the competitor is targeting also invites margin erosion we cannot sustain. Referral incentive (memory_57) is a real option but it was validated in established customers and does nothing for the two metrics actually declining. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is sound but off-cycle for this week's problem.

I want the archive records for memory_86 and memory_31 because they are the two I am actually leaning on and they are the two most likely to be over-generalized. Key unknowns: whether memory_31's day-12 result was measured long enough to be 'durable' as claimed and whether the removed fields were qualification fields; whether memory_86's completion lift came from genuine friction removal or from dropping steps that were doing real work.

Downstream value risk, flagged deliberately: cutting required signup fields improves the metric I am optimizing while potentially degrading lead qualification data, routing accuracy, and enterprise pipeline quality (memory_44's demo-request path depends on knowing who the prospect is). Completion rate can rise while qualified revenue falls. Mitigation: run as a standard experiment with retention, lead-quality, and sales-routing metrics instrumented as guardrails, not just completion and activation, and hold a later-cycle readout before any broad rollout. All inherited findings predate the competitor's entry pricing and the current QoQ declines, so prior effect sizes should be treated as directional rather than as forecasts.
